`hooks/command-safety.sh` first refuses recognized unfiltered environment dumps independently of project policy, cwd and Git. Direct named grep permission requires proven newline records; known raw NUL reads need the literal NUL-to-newline tr conversion. Flattened or unproved producer output cannot gain permission. Known nested dumps can refuse conservatively. The project-pattern check separately rejects text matching `COMMAND_SAFETY_DENY_PATTERN`, read raw and with continuations joined, including quoted text. Nonmatching text passes only that pattern check. An absent setting applies the default systemd-run memory-cap pattern; `^$` disables only pattern matching. Missing payload readers or unreadable input warn and allow the call. Empty or invalid patterns and unavailable policy tools, settings or installed support warn and allow only the pattern check.
